newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler expected to report profit after record loss in '95.
newsitem.headline: Daimler expected to report profit after record loss in '95.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG, which last year posted the highest loss ever at a German company, is expected to report a profit for the first half of the year on Thursday.

Analysts said they expect Daimler, Germany's largest conglomorate, to report a net profit of between 600 million and 700 million marks ($407 million and $475 million), which would be a record recovery from a 5.7 billion mark ($3.9 billion) loss last year.
"Daimler is on the right track," said analyst Klaus-Juergen Melzner at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts expect sales to increase about 9 percent from 48.04 billion marks ($32.6 billion) in the first half of 1995.
The company, which is trying to make its shares more attractive to investors, will report its results according to U.S. accounting standards.
Nearly all the gains will come from Daimler's truck and car division, Mercedes-Benz, which some expect to report a first-half profit of around 1.49 million marks ($1.0 million).
Analysts said a stronger dollar and sales of its E-class model, which accounts for the largest share of Mercedes car sales, are fuelling better results at Mercedes.
"The Mercedes car division is going gang busters," said Stephen Reitman, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Mercedes trucks, which face a difficult market, especially in western Europe, meanwhile will probably just about break even during the first half, analysts added.
However, as strong as Mercedes might be, Daimler's profits should be hurt by continuing losses at its air and space division, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, known as DASA.

DASA, which last year undertook a massive reorganization and dumped its money-losing Dutch aircraft maker Fokker NV, is still in the red as it makes further efforts to cut costs. It is profiting only slowly from a pickup in the global aircraft market.
